issues.description: Ed Valenzuela is identified in both source documents as the Chair of the Siskiyou County Board of Supervisors, but no relation links him to Siskiyou County or its Board of Supervisors.
Marcia Armstrong is identified in both documents as a Siskiyou County Supervisor, but lacks a relation connecting her to Siskiyou County.
Michael Kobseff is identified in Document 1 as a Siskiyou County Supervisor, but lacks a relation connecting him to Siskiyou County.
Mark Baird is named in both documents as leading the effort to secede and form the State of Jefferson, but has no relation connecting him to the proposed state.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a relation connecting mark_baird to state_of_jefferson with a suitable relation type such as LEADER_OF or PROPONENT_OF.

grader_history.summary: The knowledge graph accurately captures entities and exact evidence quotes across both source documents without hallucinating facts. However, it suffers from significant relation omissions: while Humboldt County supervisors are linked to their county via SUPERVISOR_OF, all three Siskiyou County supervisors (Ed Valenzuela, Marcia Armstrong, and Michael Kobseff) exist as isolated nodes with no relation linking them to Siskiyou County or its Board of Supervisors. Furthermore, secession movement leader Mark Baird is not connected to the State of Jefferson node. Adding these missing structural edges is required for a summary to correctly represent the political actors and their roles.

The extracted knowledge graph accurately captures the main entities and high-level structure of the secession effort covered in the documents. However, several relations suffer from weak evidence because the supporting quotes mention only one of the two relation endpoints (e.g., naming the person and their title 'Supervisor' without naming Siskiyou County, or referring to 'the effort'/'a new state' without naming the State of Jefferson). Expanding or replacing these quotes to include both endpoints will fully validate these facts for summarization.
